purpose: The third slice for docs/subsystems/actor-frame-parallel.md: what must be true before several threads may run the character controllers' and the AI's Havok queries at once. Three conditions are known: a thread memory and stack area per thread (Havok's stack area 0x00B47900 is one static block), the casts' frame budget in 0x0088B850 (shared counters, order-dependent), and the world used read-only (the phantom's broad-phase update 0x008DE950 changes the world, or queues a record when the world is locked). Map and refute only; nothing is rebuilt. Read knowledge/actor-frame-map.md, re/functions/0x008DE950.md and re/functions/0x008ECC60.md first. Class names come from the binary's RTTI (re/symbols/xobse.csv); Havok's SDK source is not public - a method name taken from memory of the SDK is 'unverified'.

functions.name: Havok start (thread memory and stack area)
functions.known: Pseudocode: makes a 0x2C-byte object (0x008A7060, vtable 0x00A95C70), hands it to 0x008BBA80, then calls slot 0 of the object in the thread's TLS block at +0x19C (or the global at 0x00BA7D9C) with (&0x00B47900, 0x60000). Measured: the character controller writes 0x00B47900.. in 96 % of its calls ([Timed] WritesOf, docs/subsystems/actor-frame-parallel.md).
questions: What exactly a second thread needs before it may run a Havok query: which object must sit in its TLS slot +0x19C, how that object is made and initialised, how a stack area is given to it, and what the fallback to 0x00BA7D9C means for a thread without one
Which TLS index and offset are used and where else the EXE sets that slot (other threads: the loader, the sound)
Skip the long list of class registrations; say only that it is there

functions.name: Cast wrapper with a frame budget
functions.known: Pseudocode: unless byte 0x00BA790A is set, every call counts 0x00BA7924 up and by the low 6 bits of [arg+0x24] one of 0x00BA7928/2C/30 or stores 0x00BA7934; when 0x00BA7924 exceeds 0x00B2E2F4 (or 0x00BA7928 reaches 0x1F) it sets [arg+0x50]=0 and [arg+0x44]=1.0 and skips the cast. Measured: written in 34 % of the vitals' calls, 6.6 % of detection's.
questions: The budget rule exactly: every counter, every limit, every exit, and what the caller sees when the cast is skipped
Where the counters are reset each frame (find the writer of 0x00BA7924..0x00BA7934 and of 0x00BA790A by cross-reference; it may address them through a base pointer)
What the cast itself is: which world function it calls, with which object, and everything that call path writes outside its own arguments
